Upper confidence bounds

ε-greedy explores blindly: a random arm, even one it already knows is bad. UCB explores where it is uncertain. Each arm's estimate gets a bonus that is large when the arm has been tried rarely. The agent picks the arm with the highest estimate plus bonus.

estimate $Q(a)$ upper bound $Q(a) + \text{bonus}$ ○ true $q_*(a)$

UCB vs ε-greedy

Average reward per step over 400 bandits (S&B Figure 2.4).

The maths

At step $t$, UCB picks

$$A_t = \arg\max_a \left[\, Q_t(a) + c\,\sqrt{\frac{\ln t}{N_t(a)}} \;\right]$$

An arm with $N_t(a) = 0$ counts as having an infinite bound, so every arm is tried once first.

The square root is a measure of uncertainty about $q_*(a)$:

  • Each pull of $a$ raises $N_t(a)$, so its bonus shrinks.
  • Each pull of another arm raises $t$, so the bonus of every neglected arm slowly grows.
  • $\ln t$ grows without limit but ever more slowly, so every arm is retried eventually, but less and less often.

$c$ sets how much uncertainty counts. With $c = 0$ the bonus vanishes and UCB is plain greedy.

The idea is optimism in the face of uncertainty: act as if each arm is as good as it plausibly could be. Either it really is good, or you quickly find out it isn't.
